learning_outcomes.text: Students master linear time-invariant systems and their mathematical description.
They understand the principle of generating electrical energy from different primary energy sources, as well as their essential properties, advantages, and disadvantages.
Students develop an awareness of the social and ethical responsibility in the use of non-renewable energies and recognize the potential and limitations of renewable energies.
Students have an overview of the connections between the essential components of energy supply networks and understand the resulting structures.
They master the physically based modeling of all essential equipment in electrical power engineering and can apply them safely based on suitable working techniques.
This particularly includes the fundamental mathematical equations that link the physical quantities of operating equipment and machines.

The profound technical knowledge of machines and devices (from milliwatts to megawatts) that shape our technical life is demanded in various professional fields – students acquire it, enabling them to communicate with specialists in the respective fields.

Based on the acquired knowledge, they represent sound viewpoints in the public discussion about current challenges in the context of energy and CO2 issues, for which they can argue in a well-founded manner.
They propose solutions that are objective and optimized for a given goal.

syllabus_topics: Functionality of key power plant types in relation to primary energy sources (coal, gas, oil, nuclear power, water, wind, sun, etc.)
Basic principles for transmission and distribution of electrical energy using three-wire systems (three-phase current)
Essential mathematical concepts for three-phase current (e.g., symmetrical components)
Principle of operation of electrical and electromechanical machines
Generation of DC voltages from AC or three-phase AC networks using power electronic components
Detailed description of the synchronous generator
Operating behavior of the induction machine at fixed and variable supply frequencies
Main protection and earthing concepts of energy supply networks
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The grade contributes 5/138 to the final grade.
